cases.subject: AI turbine-blade inspection controlled pilot
cases.evidence: We want to reduce the time required for engineer review of turbine-blade inspection images while maintaining defect-detection quality. We trained and tested an AI-assisted inspection approach using 2,400 engineer-labelled images from three sites. On a held-out test set it achieved 94% recall and 89% precision against engineer-labelled ground truth. Eight maintenance engineers then used the assistant in a controlled workflow trial. Average review time fell from 6 minutes to 3.5 minutes, seven of eight engineers found the recommendations useful, and approximately 160 engineer hours per month could be released at the tested workload. The Inspection Analytics Product Owner is accountable for the pilot and the Head of Service Engineering is the sponsor. Engineers retain the final inspection decision. The proposed next activity is a bounded single-site pilot with a 92% recall target, a 25% review-time reduction target, false-negative monitoring, and a documented low-confidence fallback to manual review. Live-data access will not begin until the applicable cybersecurity and data-governance controls have been completed. Please assess whether the idea is ready to move from DI1 Concept to DI2 Pilot.

cases.subject: AI-assisted internal service-request routing
cases.evidence: Service Operations receives approximately 2,500 internal service requests per month, and coordinators spend approximately 80 hours per month routing them manually. We trained an AI classifier and tested it on a held-out set of 1,500 historical requests. It achieved 93% routing accuracy. A rules-based comparator evaluated on the same held-out set achieved 95%, is easier to understand and maintain, and does not require model training or ongoing monitoring. The AI classifier performed better only on ambiguous cases representing fewer than 10% of the test data. The Service Operations Manager is the sponsor, and an accountable product owner has been identified. The team currently wants to continue with AI because the original initiative was proposed as an AI use case. We want to run the model on live requests, but we have not yet defined a bounded pilot scope, success and stop criteria, fallback behavior, or an experiment-risk assessment. Please assess readiness to move from DI1 Concept to DI2 Pilot.
